steps.title: Import Angular core modules and Next.js App Router dependencies
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and RouterModule from '@angular/router'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Angular modules for creating components and routing.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component from '@angular/core' and RouterModule from '@angular/router'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules for component creation and routing are imported.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and RouterModule is imported from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular modules for Next.js App Router functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but make sure to import both Component from '@angular/core' and RouterModule from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or missing. Please import Component from '@angular/core' and RouterModule from '@angular/router'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and export it. Use the selector 'app-root' and template '<router-outlet></router-outlet>'.
steps.hint: Remember to use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' and export the class so it can be used elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with proper Angular component structure and exported.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', template '<router-outlet></router-outlet>', and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main AppComponent with proper Angular component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have the @Component decorator with selector and template, and export the class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class isn't properly defined. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector 'app-root' and template '<router-outlet></router-outlet>', and export the class.

steps.title: Configure the component selector and template
steps.instruction: Add the @Component decorator above the AppComponent class with selector: 'app-root' and template: '<router-outlet></router-outlet>'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator imported from '@angular/core' to define the component metadata. The selector determines how the component is used in HTML, and the template defines its structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a selector 'app-root' and a template containing the router outlet for Next.js App Router navigation.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator is added with selector: 'app-root' and template: '<router-outlet></router-outlet>'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the component metadata. The selector 'app-root' will be used to embed this component, and the router outlet will handle route rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the @Component decorator, but check that both selector and template properties are correctly set as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component metadata is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add the @Component decorator with the exact selector and template values.

steps.title: Define the component's standalone property
steps.instruction: Add the standalone property set to true inside the @Component decorator configuration object.
steps.hint: In Angular, standalone components don't require NgModule declarations. Add 'standalone: true' as a property in the decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will be configured as a standalone component, which is required for compatibility with Next.js App Router's modular structure.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes 'standalone: true' as a property in its configuration object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured AppComponent as a standalone component. This is essential for Next.js App Router integration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added 'standalone: true' inside the @Component decorator object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The standalone property wasn't added correctly. Check that 'standalone: true' is placed inside the @Component decorator configuration.

steps.title: Import RouterModule in component imports
steps.instruction: Add the RouterModule to the component's imports array in the @Component decorator configuration.
steps.hint: Look for the imports property inside the @Component decorator and add RouterModule to the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have RouterModule properly imported, enabling routing functionality in this standalone component.
successCriteria: RouterModule is added to the imports array in the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added RouterModule to the component's imports, which enables routing functionality in this standalone component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure RouterModule is included in the imports array inside the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The RouterModule needs to be added to the imports array in the @Component decorator configuration. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Create a HomeComponent for the root route
steps.instruction: Create a new HomeComponent class with the @Component decorator, set standalone: true, and give it a simple template with a heading.
steps.hint: Define a new class named HomeComponent, add the @Component decorator with template and standalone properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A HomeComponent class is created with standalone: true and a basic template.
successCriteria: HomeComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, standalone: true, and a template containing a heading element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the HomeComponent with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component has the @Component decorator, standalone: true, and a template with a heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HomeComponent is not correctly defined. Check that it has the @Component decorator, standalone: true, and a template.

steps.title: Define the application routes configuration
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'routes' that defines two routes: one for the root path (empty string) that loads HomeComponent, and one for wildcard paths that redirects to the root.
steps.hint: Use the Routes type from '@angular/router' to define your routes array. Each route should be an object with path and component/redirectTo properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A routes constant is defined with proper TypeScript typing and two route definitions.
successCriteria: The routes constant is defined with Routes type, includes a root route to HomeComponent, and a wildcard route that redirects to root.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the route configuration. This sets up the basic routing structure similar to Next.js App Router's file-based routing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have both route definitions and proper TypeScript typing for the routes array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route configuration isn't quite right. Make sure you define a constant named 'routes' with two route objects using the Routes type.

steps.title: Configure RouterModule with application routes
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent's imports array, update the RouterModule import to use RouterModule.forRoot(routes) to configure the application routes.
steps.hint: Replace the plain RouterModule import with RouterModule.forRoot(routes) inside the imports array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Configuring a module with options
imports: [RouterModule.forRoot(appRoutes)]
steps.expectedOutcome: The RouterModule will be properly configured with the application routes, enabling navigation between components.
successCriteria: RouterModule.forRoot(routes) is added to the imports array in AppComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the RouterModule with the application routes. This enables the routing system to work properly in your Angular application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using RouterModule.forRoot(routes) inside the imports array, not just RouterModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The RouterModule needs to be configured with the routes. Update the imports array to use RouterModule.forRoot(routes).

steps.title: Add navigation links to demonstrate routing
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a navigation bar with two routerLink directives: one linking to the root path '/' and another linking to '/home'.
steps.hint: Use the routerLink directive in anchor tags to create navigation links. The navigation bar should be placed above the router-outlet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will include a navigation bar with two working links that demonstrate Angular routing.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template contains a <nav> element with two <a> tags using routerLink directives pointing to '/' and '/home'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added navigation links with routerLink directives. This demonstrates how to implement client-side navigation in Angular.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both routerLink directives: one for '/' and one for '/home' in anchor tags within a navigation element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links aren't properly implemented. Check that you're using routerLink directives in anchor tags and that they're placed in the AppComponent template.

steps.title: Test the Next.js App Router implementation
steps.instruction: Run the Angular application and test navigation between the Home and About routes by clicking the links.
steps.hint: Use the Angular CLI command 'ng serve' to start the development server, then open your browser to see the routing in action.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular application runs successfully, and you can navigate between Home and About routes by clicking the links.
successCriteria: Application runs without errors and navigation between routes works correctly when clicking links
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully tested the Next.js App Router implementation in Angular. The routing functionality is working correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: The application runs, but navigation might not be working as expected. Check that your route configuration and navigation links are properly set up.
steps.feedbackWrong: The application failed to run or navigation doesn't work. Verify your Angular setup, route configuration, and navigation implementation.
